items.title: ICLR paper prep: rewrite the paper around first-state (k=1) sufficiency
items.body:
# ICLR paper prep: rewrite the paper around first-state (k=1) sufficiency

Reviewer-grade gap analysis of the current k=1 / token-zero direction, done as an
ICLR reviewer would. **Headline: the paper in `paper/` is being rewritten, not
revised.** Every load-bearing section of the current draft describes the
layer-wise method we are no longer leading with.

Sources read: `docs/planning/FIRST_TOKEN_TOKENWISE_CONTRASTIVE.md`,
`docs/planning/ISSUE_156_ARCHITECTURE_SWEEP.md`,
`docs/planning/ISSUE_157_SCORER_STUDY.md`,
`docs/planning/TOKENWISE_SUPCON_FACTORIAL.md`, `results/draft_headline_table.md`,
`results/results_table.csv`, commits `4228d32..b96d6f3`, and the full `paper/` tree.

---

## 0. Numbers this analysis rests on

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| v1 token-wise (`t0 + later token`), 5-dataset KNN macro | 0.7790 | `ISSUE_156_ARCHITECTURE_SWEEP.md:16` |
| t0 dropout control (`t0 + t0`), 5-dataset KNN macro | 0.7751 | same |
| v1 linear-probe macro | 0.7590 | same |
| t0 control linear-probe macro | 0.7719 | same |
| v2 depth-norm/projection trunk macro | 0.6947 | same, Stage 0 table |
| ACT-ViT @ k=1, macro | 0.757 | reported verbally; **not located in-repo** |
| Full-response layer-wise contrastive, Llama 5 free-form macro | 0.8116 | computed from `results/draft_headline_table.md` |
| ACT-ViT full-response, Llama 5 free-form macro | 0.7972 | same (searchqa 3/5, mmlu 2/5 seeds incomplete) |

**Action:** the ACT-ViT@k=1 = 0.757 figure could not be found in `results/` or
`docs/`. Land it in a tracked artifact before it is cited anywhere.

---

## 1. Does this pass the ICLR novelty bar? Yes — but on a different claim than the method

**What clears the bar: detection strictly before generation.** Every method in
our baseline grid reads the response. SAPLMA reads a generated statement;
ACT-ViT reads the full `(L x N x D)` response tensor; SE and SelfCheckGPT need K
sampled responses; INSIDE reads response states. Our detector reads `S_0`, the
prefill state at the last prompt position, which conditions on no response
token. "Hallucination risk is legible before the model has said anything" is a
clean, falsifiable claim on an axis no cited work occupies.

This is a materially stronger novelty position than the layer-wise draft's
"layer pairs as contrastive views," which should be abandoned rather than
rewritten (see §5).

**The theoretical framing is also much stronger than the layer-wise `§3.2`.**
`I(C;S_{0:T-1}) - I(C;S_0) ~ 0` is a real quantity with a real estimator
(`Delta_t = AUROC(Z_t) - AUROC(Z_0)`), predeclared as falsifying. The KV-cache
argument (two parallel prompt-dependent paths `X -> H_0` and `X -> K_0`, so
`H_0(X)=H_0(X')` does not imply `K_0(X)=K_0(X')`) is exactly the objection a
good reviewer raises, and we raise it ourselves. The "injectivity would make
`H_0` formally sufficient via arbitrary inverse lookup, which is technically
valid but scientifically weak" passage earns reviewer trust.

### Do not oversell Theorem 1

Under greedy decoding, Theorem 1 reduces to "a deterministic function of the
prompt is determined by the prompt." A reviewer will say so in one line. The
doc already concedes this ("under deterministic greedy decoding, the
distribution is a point mass"), but the "strongest defensible paper claim" box
still leads with the theorem.

- [ ] Lead with the **empirical** hypothesis (recorded-`S_0` sufficiency); keep
      Theorem 1 as the half-page that pins down *what functional* is estimated.
- [ ] Add one sentence conceding Theorem 1 is exact for `C_64`, a substring-match
      proxy — the theorem's precision is about the benchmark contract, not about
      hallucination.
- [ ] Theorem 2's `epsilon` is currently **unmeasurable** from our captures (64-token
      captures terminate at the boundary, so the early-answer tail cannot be
      estimated). Either measure it on a few hundred uncapped generations, or cut
      Theorem 2.

---

## 2. BLOCKER: our own control undercuts the mechanism claim

From `ISSUE_156_ARCHITECTURE_SWEEP.md:16`:

| Recipe | KNN macro | Linear-probe macro |
|---|---:|---:|
| v1 (`t0 + later token`) — the treatment | 0.7790 | 0.7590 |
| t0 (`t0 + t0` dropout) — the control | 0.7751 | **0.7719** |

**The temporal mechanism buys +0.39 AUROC points on KNN and loses 1.29 points on
the linear surface.** That is a wash, and the sign flip across scoring surfaces
is worse than a wash: it suggests the difference is scorer geometry, not
information.

This directly contradicts the mechanism story in
`FIRST_TOKEN_TOKENWISE_CONTRASTIVE.md` — that later-token states supply
privileged supervision teaching the encoder to expose signal latent in `S_0`.
The predeclared 3-arm causal comparison is the right instrument and arm 2 has
already come back negative.

- [ ] Add to the doc's falsification criteria: **"gains disappear against the t0
      dropout control."** That is what the current data shows.

### Required reframe — split the claims

- **Claim A (strong, supported).** Hallucination risk is substantially
  recoverable from the pre-response state: ~0.779 macro at token zero against
  ~0.812 for full-response layer-wise contrastive on the same five Llama
  datasets — roughly **96% of full-response AUROC available before the first
  token exists.** This is the headline and it holds regardless of how the
  encoder is trained.
- **Claim B (weak, currently unsupported).** Token-wise contrastive with
  later-token views is the way to extract it. Current data says any reasonable
  contrastive encoder on the `t=0` cross-layer stack gets there.

Lead with A. Report B honestly, negative if it stays negative — a clean "the
temporal view does not beat the dropout control" is publishable content and is
consistent with the honesty that makes the rest of the doc strong. The
`TOKENWISE_SUPCON_FACTORIAL.md` view x recon 2x2 is the right instrument, but at
one seed with a 0.4-point margin it decides nothing.

---

## 3. Do we beat SOTA fairly and sufficiently at k=1? Not yet

The +2.2 over ACT-ViT@k=1 has a problem unrelated to its size: **ACT-ViT at k=1
is a baseline we constructed by crippling a method designed for the full
response tensor.** A reviewer will call it a strawman. The fix is not a bigger
margin; it is baselines that are natural at token zero.

- [ ] **Raw-`S_0` linear / MLP probe on all five datasets — highest priority.**
      Logistic probe directly on the `(32 x 4096)` token-zero stack, no
      contrastive training. Our learned-embedding linear-probe macros are
      0.759–0.772; if a raw-`S_0` probe lands near 0.77, the entire contrastive
      apparatus is unjustified. A reviewer will run this thought experiment
      whether or not we run the experiment.
- [ ] **P(IK) (Kadavath et al. 2022)** as a baseline — see §4.
- [ ] **P(true) asked before answering**, as a prompt-only output-space floor.
- [ ] Per-dataset win/loss across all cells instead of a macro; paired
      significance across the five seeds.
- [ ] State the **exact parameter match** prominently — `77,538,112` params,
      identical to the layer-wise encoder because the progressive compressor is
      sequence-length agnostic. "The parameter-controlled test changes the data
      geometry, not capacity" is a sentence reviewers reward. Extend the same
      treatment to the ACT-ViT comparison (parameter/FLOP column).

### Scorer-selection hygiene

`ISSUE_157_SCORER_STUDY.md` is above the norm for this literature — nine
predeclared candidates, validation-only selection, a manifest certifying test
arrays were never opened. Describe it in the paper rather than burying it.

- [ ] Close the one soft spot the doc already flags: validation does double duty
      for checkpoint selection *and* scorer selection. Reserve a distinct
      scorer-calibration split before submission or reviewers will price in the leak.

---

## 4. Related work — one existential threat, one free win

**Threat — `P(IK)` in Kadavath et al. 2022.** We already cite this paper for
logprob / entropy / P(true) but not for P(IK): a head trained to predict whether
the model will answer correctly, evaluated *before* the answer is sampled. That
is pre-generation correctness prediction — our headline axis. Unaddressed, this
is a rejection. Addressed head-on it is a strength. Differentiators to state:
P(IK) requires finetuning the LM itself and reads an output-space scalar; ours
is a frozen-activation probe over the full cross-layer stack with a formal
statement of which functional is estimated.

**Free win — Learning Using Privileged Information.** The doc uses the phrase
"privileged training information" for later-token states and cites only Shannon,
Tishby, and Bengio. LUPI (Vapnik & Vashist 2009) and generalized distillation
(Lopez-Paz et al. 2016) are the established frame for training with information
unavailable at test time. One sentence; gives Claim B a principled home even if
the effect stays small.

**Citation candidates to verify (per `references.bib` policy — no agent may
insert these; human approval required):**

- [ ] Kadavath et al. 2022 — P(IK) specifically, distinct from the P(true) cite we have
- [ ] Vapnik & Vashist 2009 (LUPI); Lopez-Paz et al. 2016 (generalized distillation)
- [ ] Yin et al. 2023 (SelfAware) — prompt-only answerability
- [ ] Snyder et al. KDD 2024 — early detection of hallucinations in factual QA
- [ ] INSIDE / EigenScore, ICLR 2024 — internal-state single-pass detector, ICLR-native
- [ ] HaloScope, NeurIPS 2024
- [ ] Deep SVDD (Ruff et al. 2018), CSI (Tack et al. 2020) — one-class anomaly framing,
      still relevant since the asymmetric `ignore_label` scheme is retained token-wise
- [ ] Tschannen et al. ICLR 2020 (*On Mutual Information Maximization*) — only if any
      InfoNCE-bounds-MI argument survives into the rewrite

---

## 5. Paper rewrite scope — `paper/` is stale, not merely out of date

`grep -ri "tokenwise|token-wise|token pair|first-state" paper/` returns **zero
matches**. Last paper commit is `a7676cb`. The following are describing a method
we are no longer leading with:

| File / section | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `sections/00_abstract.tex`, `01_intro.tex` | placeholder + layer-wise framing | rewrite around Claim A |
| `02_related_work.md` §2.3 | novelty staked on "layer pairs as views" | **replace** with the pre-generation axis; add §4 citations |
| `02_related_work.md` §2.2 | no P(IK), no INSIDE / HaloScope | extend |
| `03_method.md` §3.2 | MI feasibility argument ("our loss descends") | **delete**; replace with first-state sufficiency + `Delta_t` |
| `03_method.md` §3.3 | layer-pair views, mean-pool over `T_y` | rewrite: token-zero cross-layer stack, depth-axis encoder |
| `03_method.md` §3.4 | 2x2 SupCon x recon attribution over the layer-wise method | re-target to the token-wise factorial |
| `04_experimental_setup.md` §4.3 | K=1 means "one forward pass" | **terminology collision** — K=1-forward-pass vs. k=1-first-token. Pick distinct names now, before either reaches prose |
| `outline.md` §7.3 (layer-pair sensitivity) | obsolete | replace with the `t=0,1,3,7,15,31,63` `Delta_t` diagnostic curve |
| `theory_outline.md` | superseded twice over | delete |
| `paper/data/baseline_comparison.csv` | still the 2026-05-18 placeholder | regenerate from the k=1 results once they land |

Also note the §2.3 "broad novelty" verdict (resolved 2026-05-19) is moot — it was
scoped to the cross-layer view claim. Do not carry a broad claim into the
rewrite; the pre-generation axis is defensible narrowly and does not need it.

---

## 6. Ranked actions

0. **ACT-ViT trained at k=1, evaluated at k=1** (added 2026-08-18). The current
   75.7 is a prefix-trained checkpoint extrapolating from `k>=8`; we train at our
   deployment point and the baseline does not. Can erase the +2.2. See §8.3.
1. **Raw-`S_0` linear/MLP probe, five datasets.** Decides whether we have a
   method paper or a finding paper. Cheap, no new capture.
2. **Multi-seed confirmation of v1 vs. t0-dropout.** At a 0.4-point margin one
   seed decides nothing; this determines whether Claim B survives at all.
3. **Add P(IK) baseline + citation.** Closes the existential related-work threat.
4. **Reframe the narrative**: lead with "~96% of full-response AUROC before
   generation begins"; report the temporal-view result honestly.
5. Per-cell win/loss + paired tests; parameter/FLOP column across all k=1 methods.
6. Land ACT-ViT@k=1 = 0.757 in a tracked artifact.
7. Measure Theorem 2's `epsilon` on uncapped generations, or cut Theorem 2.
8. Distinct scorer-calibration split.
9. Execute the `paper/` rewrite table in §5.

## Assessment

- **Novelty:** clears the ICLR bar on Claim A. Not on the contrastive method.
- **SOTA:** not fairly established yet; the raw-`S_0` probe is the deciding experiment.
- **Related work:** one serious gap (P(IK)), otherwise fixable.


---

## 7. Design decision: two-point k comparison, no mixed-prefix training

Scope decision for the ACT-ViT comparison, given that the rewrite strips the
temporal (later-token view) component and the layer-wise contrastive views.
Companion note posted on #149.

### 7.1 Why skipping mixed-prefix training is justified, not a shortcut

#149's matched multi-k protocol exists because its headline arm (`prefix_mixed`)
constructs positive views that **differ in prefix**. Prefix length is therefore
part of that method's training distribution, which forces a choice of training
support over `k` and obliges every baseline to receive the same support — hence
the multi-k sampler, global geometry selection, and per-k oracle arms.

Strip the temporal and layer-wise view construction and no k-dependent view
machinery remains. The method becomes an encoder over the activation tensor
available at a single fixed `k`. There is no prefix distribution to match, so
the fairness contract reduces to the ordinary one: same `k`, same rows, same
split seeds, same training seeds.

**Mixed-prefix training is not skipped; it is inapplicable.** State it that way
in the paper and in any rebuttal.

### 7.2 Verified: k=1 is a genuinely matched comparison

`build_prefix_mask(prefix_len=1)` retains exactly index 0
(`activation_research/prefix_views.py:439-464`). Per the capture semantics in
`FIRST_TOKEN_TOKENWISE_CONTRASTIVE.md`, `response_activations[:, 0, :]` is the
prefill state at the final prompt position and conditions on no sampled response
token.

**#149's `k=1` and the first-token doc's `t=0` are therefore the same tensor
slice.** ACT-ViT@k=1 and the token-wise encoder receive identical input. The
77.9 / 75.7 comparison is apples-to-apples.

`k=1` is also the only point on the grid where "prefix `<= k`" and "position
`k`" coincide (one column either way), which is what makes it free of the
aggregation-semantics ambiguity described next.

### 7.3 k=64 is the problematic point — not the skipped middle

At `k=64` the two readings diverge:

- ACT-ViT at prefix 64 pools the entire `(layer, token)` plane — 64 columns.
- The stripped method reads a depth stack at *a* position.

If the stripped method aggregates tokens `1..64` it becomes ACT-ViT-shaped and
the architectural distinction narrows to pooling details. If it reads only
column 64, ACT-ViT sees 64x the input and the comparison is unmatched in the
opposite direction from `k=1`.

**Decision: `k=64` is a reference ceiling, not a matched arm.** This is already
the framing in `FIRST_TOKEN_TOKENWISE_CONTRASTIVE.md`'s primary comparison
(arm 3, "full-response current contrastive encoder as the information-rich
reference"). Keep that wording. Matched ACT-ViT **training** is then required
only at `k=1`; the `k=64` column is the existing full-response result
establishing the ceiling that `k=1` recovers ~96% of.

One competitive point plus one reference point is cheaper and more honest than
two half-matched claims.

### 7.4 What the skipped middle costs, and the mitigation

Lost: the shape of `Delta_t` — whether information accrues smoothly across
generation or the model commits late. A reviewer may fairly ask.

Mitigation is cheap because the asymmetry favors us: **evaluating our encoder at
other `k` requires no retraining** (already specified as the `t=0,1,3,7,15,31,63`
diagnostic curve). It is *baseline* retraining at every `k` that is expensive.

- [ ] Report our own full evaluation curve as a diagnostic — "deployment stress"
      in #149's taxonomy.
- [ ] Do matched training only at `k=1`.
- [ ] Label the asymmetry explicitly; it is defensible only if named.

### 7.5 Consequences

- [ ] **Rigor bar rises.** With a 7-point curve, consistency across `k` carries
      the argument. With one competitive point, +2.2 stands on per-dataset
      win/loss and paired significance alone. Reinforces action 5 in §6.
- [ ] **Scope out #149's framing in one explicit sentence.** "How early can
      hallucination be predicted" is #149's paper. Without that sentence a
      reviewer reads our two points as a thin version of it.
- [ ] **Dropped from the critical path:** #149 Waves B–D — multi-k retraining for
      linear probe, SAPLMA, ICR feature recomputation, per-k LLMsKnow sweeps, the
      ACT-ViT multi-k sampler, and global geometry selection.
- [ ] **Retained:** one new training job (ACT-ViT at `k=1`, matched) plus existing
      full-response numbers as the reference ceiling.


---

## 8. Decision: ACT-ViT arms in the paper, and privileged-information fairness

Extends §7. Settles which ACT-ViT arms the paper reports, and reframes the
`TOKENWISE_SUPCON_FACTORIAL` from confound-resolution to fairness-determining.

### 8.1 If the temporal component stays, is mixed-prefix ACT-ViT required?

**No — it is matched on the wrong axis.**

#149's protocol matches **evaluation across k**: `prefix_mixed` trains over a
prefix distribution *and is evaluated* at varying prefix, so matched training
support is genuinely required there.

Temporal token-wise is different. Later-token states are used **at training time
only**; inference sees `S_0` alone, and deployment `k` is fixed at 1 for both us
and ACT-ViT. The asymmetry is in what the *trainer* saw, not what the detector
reads at test time. That is Learning Using Privileged Information (see §4), not
prefix-awareness. A mixed-prefix ACT-ViT would match us on an axis where we
claim no advantage and leave us unmatched on the one where we do.

### 8.2 The privileged-information ladder — and `L_recon` is privileged too

The reviewer objection is real: *you trained using the full response, deploy at
token zero, and compare against a baseline that never saw past token zero.*

Easy to miss: **`L_recon` is also privileged information.** It regresses the full
64-token logprob trajectory from a single-step representation — a target
unavailable at deployment. So the t0-dropout control (0.7751) is **not** a
privilege-free arm.

`TOKENWISE_SUPCON_FACTORIAL.md` is therefore not only a confound experiment; it
is the fairness ladder:

| Arm | Later-token views | Full-response recon | Privileged |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v1` (t0+tn, recon) — current 77.9 | yes | yes | fully |
| `tokenwise_supcon_t0_full_recon` | no | yes | partially |
| `tokenwise_supcon_tn_no_recon` | yes | no | partially |
| **`tokenwise_supcon_t0_no_recon`** | no | no | **none** |

**`tokenwise_supcon_t0_no_recon` vs. ACT-ViT@k=1 is the strictly-matched
comparison.** Every arm above it is privileged relative to that baseline and must
be disclosed as such. (The `C_64` label derives from the full response for both
methods — symmetric, not part of the asymmetry.)

The current 77.9 vs 75.7 headline is the *fully privileged* arm against an
unprivileged baseline. That is the live exposure.

- [ ] Run the factorial to five seeds **before** locking the headline comparison.
      Which rung the method stands on determines which baseline framing is honest.
- [ ] If the temporal gain stays ~0 across seeds (current one-seed evidence:
      +0.39 KNN, -1.29 linear), the ladder collapses, no privileged-information
      advantage exists to neutralize, and ACT-ViT@k=1 is fair with no extra arms.
      The control that undercuts Claim B also discharges the fairness objection.
- [ ] If the temporal gain is real and survives seeds, the honest headline becomes
      "with privileged training-time supervision, 77.9 at token zero vs 75.7 for a
      baseline trained without it" — still a fine claim, stated in those words.

### 8.3 REVISED 2026-08-18 — the 75.7 is the prefix-trained arm

**Correction.** `75.7` is ACT-ViT **prefix-trained, evaluated at k=1** — the
*strongest* arm available, not the weakest. Two consequences, one good and one
worse than anything in the previous revision.

**Good: the reserve/footnote question is void.** There is no stronger withheld
baseline, so nothing is being held back and no disclosure decision is needed.
The current +2.2 is already measured against the hardest ACT-ViT we have. Delete
the guardrails about "held for rebuttal" — they addressed a situation that does
not exist.

**Worse: ACT-ViT trained at k=1 has never been run, and the arm we do have is
extrapolating outside its training support.**

The prefix sampler defaults to `prefix_min_tokens=8` with `prefix_min_gap=8`
(`activation_research/training.py:907,1682`), so the prefix-trained checkpoint
**never sees k<8**. #149 states this outright and prescribes the fix:

> Consequently, `k=1/4` are extrapolation points in the current pilot. They are
> still fair if every multi-k competitor uses the identical training support. If
> `k=1/4` become headline matched-training results, both HalluLens and the
> learned baselines must receive an additional low-k training arm.

`k=1` *is* now our headline matched-training result, so that conditional has
fired.

The degradation is likely material, not marginal: ACT-ViT adaptive-pools the
`(layer, token)` plane to `(L_p=8, N_p=100)` (`configs/methods/act_vit.json`).
At `k=1` a single column is pooled to `N_p=100` — a degenerate regime the
checkpoint never trained for. **75.7 is plausibly an underestimate of what
ACT-ViT can do at k=1.**

Meanwhile the token-wise method is *first-anchored* — `k=0` appears in the pair
on every update — so it trains **at its deployment point**. Stated plainly:
**we trained at k=1 and the baseline did not.** That is the same strawman
objection as before, arriving from a direction we had not checked, and it is the
largest single risk to the SOTA claim.

| Arm | Status | Role |
|---|---|---|
| ACT-ViT prefix-trained, eval k=1 (**75.7**) | have | current headline competitor — but extrapolating from `k>=8` |
| **ACT-ViT trained k=1, eval k=1** | **NOT RUN** | the arm the claim actually requires |
| ACT-ViT trained k=64, eval k=64 | have | reference ceiling (§7.3) |
| ACT-ViT trained k=64, eval k=1 | have, worse than prefix | excluded — see §8.4 |

- [ ] **Train ACT-ViT at k=1 and evaluate at k=1. This is now the top-priority
      experiment for the SOTA claim.** It can erase the +2.2 outright; no framing
      decision downstream of it is safe until it lands.
- [ ] If it does erase the margin, the paper is not dead — Claim A (first-state
      detectability, ~96% of ceiling before generation) is architecture-agnostic
      and survives an ACT-ViT that matches us at k=1. The SOTA framing would
      change, not the finding.
- [ ] Retire the "we tune baselines to their best" guardrail as moot, but keep
      the factual-protocol wording rule from the previous revision.

### 8.4 Why the deployment-stress arm is excluded

`k64 -> k1` also had full-response training access, so beating it looks like
evidence that our transfer mechanism works. It is not, unless one diagnostic
comes back the right way:

- If `k64->k1` **<** `k1->k1`: full-response training *hurt* it at token zero. It
  is a model suffering input-distribution shift (ACT-ViT adaptively pools the
  `(layer, token)` plane; 64 columns vs. 1 gives very different pooled
  statistics), not a privileged-information null. Beating it supports only
  "ACT-ViT does not survive truncation" — a robustness observation, not mechanism
  evidence. Expected outcome.
- If `k64->k1` **>=** `k1->k1`: legitimate privileged-information null, and
  beating it is real mechanism evidence. Would justify promoting it to a panel.

- [ ] Run the `k64->k1` vs `k1->k1` diagnostic before discarding the arm
      permanently — it is an evaluation-only comparison on existing checkpoints.

### 8.5 What the paper does not narrate

Deliberate scoping, recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for an
oversight. None of the following is owed to a reader, and all of it is expensive
to explain for a claim we are not making:

- #149 itself, the prefix grid, the three comparison regimes, the multi-k
  fairness protocol;
- intermediate `k` points and the early-detection framing ("how early can
  hallucination be predicted" is #149's paper, not ours — see §7.5);
- that mixed-prefix training was ever a design consideration.

### 8.6 RESOLVED — which arm is the 75.7

Answered 2026-08-18: prefix-trained, evaluated at `k=1`. See §8.3 for the
consequences. The remaining artifact task from §0 still stands — land the
ACT-ViT k=1 numbers (prefix-trained, and the k=1-trained arm once it exists) in
a tracked file rather than carrying them verbally.


---

## 9. CONSOLIDATED DESIGN (2026-08-18) — supersedes §7 and §8.3

Two things are scrapped from the paper entirely:

- **The prefix / multi-k line of thinking.** We never ran k=1 prefix *training*,
  the prefix-trained checkpoint extrapolates from `k>=8` (§8.3), and the framing
  contributes nothing to the claim while inviting reviewer questions about a
  curve we are not reporting.
- **The layer-wise contrastive method** (layer-pair views, full-response
  encoder). Not the paper's method; its presence forces §2.3's dead novelty
  claim and §3.2's dead MI argument back into scope.

Sections §7 and §8.3 are retained as history — the reasoning is still what
justifies the scoping — but the design below is what ships.

### 9.1 Framing: drop the `k` notation

Two conditions, named in plain language:

| Condition | Definition |
|---|---|
| **pre-generation** | detector observes only the state preceding the first response token (`response_activations[:, 0, :]`, the prefill state at the final prompt position) |
| **full-response** | detector observes the complete 64-token generation |

No `k`, no prefix vocabulary, no implied curve. "k=1 vs k=64" invites *"why not
the points in between?"*; "pre-generation vs full-response" does not.

**Keep the prefix masking code** (`activation_research/prefix_views.py`) — it is
required to produce ACT-ViT's pre-generation evaluation. Implementation detail,
not narrative.

### 9.2 Ceiling anchor no longer depends on a method of ours

Scrapping the layer-wise contrastive removes the 0.8116 full-response anchor that
0.7790 was "96% of". Re-anchor to the **best full-response baseline**:

`0.7790 / 0.7972 = 97.7%` (ACT-ViT full-response, Llama, five free-form datasets)

Stated entirely in terms of published baselines and depending on no method of
ours: *a pre-generation detector reaches ~98% of the best full-response
detector's AUROC.* Stronger and more robust than the previous phrasing.

- [ ] Carry the caveat: ACT-ViT's SearchQA cell is 3/5 seeds in
      `results/draft_headline_table.md`. Complete it or state the incompleteness.

### 9.3 Baseline grid

**Pre-generation condition (the headline comparison):**

| Baseline | Status |
|---|---|
| Ours (token-wise SupCon encoder on the `S_0` depth stack) | have (0.7790) |
| **Linear on flattened 32x4096 `S_0` stack** | **NOT RUN — decisive; see §6** |
| Linear on a single layer's `S_0` | not run — direct analogue of the existing linear-probe row |
| **ACT-ViT trained pre-generation, eval pre-generation** | **NOT RUN — top priority, §8.3** |
| ACT-ViT trained full-response, eval pre-generation | have; worse than the prefix arm |
| SAPLMA at `t0` (MLP on single-layer `S_0`) | not run — capacity control |
| LLMsKnow at `t0` (reduces to a layer sweep) | not run |
| First-token entropy / logprob | not run — the *right* output-space baseline for a pre-generation claim; current entropy/logprob rows are full-response |
| P(IK) (Kadavath) | not run — the only published method making a pre-generation correctness prediction; conspicuous in this framing (§4) |
| ICR probe | skip + disclose (0.675 reproduction, §3) |

**ACT-ViT arms — all four in one place, to end the ambiguity:**

| Arm | In paper? | Role |
|---|---|---|
| trained pre-gen, eval pre-gen | **yes** | matched headline competitor — **NOT RUN** |
| trained full-response, eval pre-gen | **yes** | deployment stress; have it, worse than the prefix arm |
| **trained full-response, eval full-response** | **yes** | **reference ceiling — the 0.7972 anchoring the 97.7% claim (§9.2)** |
| prefix-trained, eval pre-gen (75.7) | no | scrapped with the prefix framing; extrapolates from `k>=8` (§8.3) |

**Full-response condition (reference ceiling only, no competitive claim):**
existing grid — linear probe, SAPLMA, LLMsKnow, ACT-ViT, SE, SelfCheckGPT.

**Sampling methods are structurally excluded from the pre-generation column** —
SE and SelfCheckGPT require samples that do not yet exist at that point. State
this explicitly rather than leaving blanks; it is a point in the paper's favour,
not a coverage gap.

### 9.4 Cleanup consequences

- [ ] `results/draft_headline_table.md`'s "Contrastive+Recon (ours)" row is the
      **scrapped** layer-wise method. Do not let it survive into the paper labelled
      "ours" — the paper's method is the token-wise pre-generation encoder.
- [ ] §5 rewrite-table entries in §5 of this issue for `02_related_work.md` §2.3
      and `03_method.md` §3.2 become deletions rather than rewrites.
- [ ] Nothing in §8.2 changes: the privileged-information ladder and the
      five-seed factorial still gate the headline, independently of this scoping.

items.title: [Bugfix][AMD] A GPU-CPU KV transfer fault in OffloadingConnector takes the engine down instead of degrading the cache.
items.body:
## Purpose swap_blocks_batch raises synchronously inside transfer_async — STD_TORCH_CHECK(result == hipSuccess, ...) at csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu:168 on the ROCm path, and the equivalent check at :151 on the CUDA path. A device error latched by earlier work on the transfer stream surfaces the same way at end_event.query(). Every call site is unguarded, so that exception reaches execute_model and kills the worker: - V1 (kv_connector_model_runner_mixin.py) calls start_load_kv at :95, one line above the try: at :96. - V2 (v1/worker/gpu/kv_connector.py) has no try at all in pre_forward (:61) or post_forward (:77). - gpu_model_runner.handle_preemptions, which submits stores and waits on them, is also unguarded. Meanwhile the failure channel that exists is dead code. offloading/worker.py:359 carries the comment "we currently do not support job failures" above assert transfer_result.success, and the only producer of that result hardcodes success=True (v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:691). OffloadingConnector also does not override get_block_ids_with_load_errors, so base.py's empty-set default applies and the scheduler's _handle_invalid_blocks recovery is unreachable for this connector — even though the plumbing is already wired at v1/worker/gpu/kv_connector.py:89. This is the wrong failure mode for this connector in particular. offloading_connector.py:56 returns requires_kv_delivery = False with the comment "a dropped save is just a future cache miss, so opt out of the producer-role default". It declares best-effort delivery and then aborts the engine when a transfer fails. What this changes Faults are reported, not raised: - transfer_async catches the fault, queues the job as a submit failure, and still returns True. Jobs must always complete: the scheduler's per-job pending count waits for world_size acks, so a job that silently disappears strands the request forever. The stream and events are deliberately not returned to their pools — a latched device error would otherwise leak into an unrelated transfer. The pinned descriptor buffers are plain host memory and are still recycled. - get_finished drains submit failures and guards end_event.query() / elapsed_time, emitting TransferResult(success=False). - wait() no longer propagates a synchronize failure; the next poll reports it, keeping failure handling in one place. - A failed store is dropped with a warning. The chunk is simply not cached — exactly what requires_kv_delivery = False already promises. - A failed load is escalated. Its destination GPU blocks hold undefined data while the scheduler has already advanced num_computed_tokens past them, so resuming the request would read garbage KV. The blocks are reported through a newly implemented get_block_ids_with_load_errors() and the scheduler recomputes them. The request is still reported via get_finished(), as the base-class contract requires. Not a duplicate - #50984 implements the same reporting pattern for the Mooncake connector. Different connector, no overlap; it is a useful precedent that this is the accepted shape. - #42461 would replace the per-block error API (invalid_block_ids / get_block_ids_with_load_errors) with a per-request one. Its RFC, #35780, was auto-closed as stale / not-planned on 2026-08-18, and the per-request API is not on main. The per-block API is therefore still the live interface. If #42461 ever lands, this connector migrates alongside nixl, mooncake, flexkv, lmcache and multi_connector, so this adds no migration burden. ## Test Plan 1. run existing kv_offload in CI ## Test Result Some tests in the sweep already known to fail. The change only adds passed tests ---
Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

items.title: The record-anchor symbol test accepts a COMMENT that names the symbol, so a citation 70 lines off its declaration reads OK — and the two-way ratchet then forces the next commit to bank a repair nobody made
items.body:
The record-anchor ratchet (`ENG-RECORD-ANCHOR-RATCHET`, #632) classifies a citation
`STALE` when the cited lines do not contain the symbol named beside it. The test is a
substring search over those lines. A **comment** that mentions the symbol therefore
satisfies it, so a citation can pass while pointing nowhere near the thing it names.

## The live instance

`KERNEL-ATTN-MLA-SPARSE` cites `include/vllm/v1/attention/backend.h:271` for
`get_kv_cache_shape`. The file is 431 lines. Line 271 is a comment:

```
// Upstream rocm_attn.py:247-256 (`get_kv_cache_shape`) returns
```

The real declaration is 70 lines further down, at `:341`:

```
  std::vector<int64_t> get_kv_cache_shape(
      int64_t num_blocks, int64_t block_size, int64_t num_kv_heads,
```

Drift on `main` moved that ROCm comment onto `:271`. The citation now reads `OK`, and
nothing repaired it. `.agents/specs/record-anchor-ratchet.md` §`Our baseline` records
this honestly as a **measured limit** of the conservative rule rather than as a repair,
and that framing is right: separating a declaration from a comment needs a parser per
language, which is the cry-wolf trade the whole design refuses
(`scripts/check-agent-record.py`, the `WHERE THE CONSERVATIVE LINE IS DRAWN` block).

So this is not a request to tighten the symbol test by parsing. It is a request to make
the false negative visible, because of what it costs downstream.

## The second-order cost, which the spec does not currently draw out

The ratchet fails in **both** directions. A bucket above its baseline fails, and a bucket
below it fails too, with the instruction to lower the baseline in the same commit as the
repair that earned it. That rule exists so improvements are banked rather than silently
absorbed, and it is correct as long as a fall means a repair.

A fall does not always mean a repair. Unrelated drift that parks a comment naming the
symbol on a cited line lowers the count with no work done, and the next contributor to
touch the tree is then **forced to bank an improvement that never happened**. The banked
number is permanent, because the baseline only ever moves down.

This is not hypothetical. It happened while `row/anchor-ratchet-impl` merged `main`:

- `72bd06a5a` (`record(ROAD-V1-C6)`, #535) is a record reconciliation that touches no
  `src/`, `include/` or `tests/` file. It rewrote the `SERVE-ASYNC-LLM` row and replaced
  the citation `` `examples/server/main.cpp:230-247` `` with a bare
  `` `examples/server/main.cpp` ``.
- That citation was `BROKEN` (the file is 23 lines). Dropping the line number did not
  repair it; it removed the anchor, so the ratchet stopped counting it.
- `broken` fell 7 to 6. The ratchet then went red on the fall, and the merge commit had
  to lower the baseline to 6 to go green — banking an improvement nobody made, on a row
  that had nothing to do with `SERVE-ASYNC-LLM`.

The same mechanism runs through the `STALE` bucket via the comment case above, and there
it is harder to see, because the citation still looks anchored.

## What would close this

Not a per-language parser. Candidates, in increasing cost:

1. `--report` marks a citation whose only match is inside a comment, so the false
   negative is legible without changing any verdict or count.
2. `--write-baseline` refuses, or warns loudly, when the fall is not attributable to a
   citation the same commit edited. That is the property actually wanted: a bank should
   name the repair that earned it.
3. A cheap non-parser heuristic, for example preferring a match on a line that is not
   inside a `//` or `#` prefix when the file offers both.

None of these is in scope for #632, which lands the ratchet itself.

## Not a duplicate

- #911 is the different gap that **spec bodies** are not policed at all. This one is
  about citations the ratchet does read and rules `OK` for the wrong reason.
- #632 owns the ratchet's landing. This is the residual false negative the landing
  measured and recorded.
- #1270 is the `--write-baseline` ordering bug, already fixed.

Owning row: `ENG-RECORD-ANCHOR-RATCHET`.
